summary: The help handling is correct and well tested. VALUE_OPTIONS matches every string option defined across all seven parseArgs calls (no short options exist); -h/--help is honored before `--`, ignored as an option value (`--path --help`) and in `--opt=value` form, and ignored after `--`. Unknown options still exit 1. Three non-blocking observations on maintainability, an edge case, and test gaps.
overseer_note: Someone asked for `node src/cli.js gate check --help` to print usage instead of failing. The change adds a small scanner in src/cli.js that runs before any command logic: it prints the usage text and exits 0 when it sees -h or --help, but skips over flags that take values (like --path) so `evidence --path --help` still fails as before, and stops at `--` so arguments after it are never treated as help. I checked the scanner's list of value-taking flags against every command's real flag definitions by hand; they match exactly today, and no command uses short flags, so there is no drift. I also checked tricky inputs: `--task=--help` (no false help), `validate -- --help` (fails, no help), and an unknown command. Tests cover all 16 command/subcommand forms with both flags, the option-value case, the `--` case, and the unknown-option case, and they would fail if the new logic were removed. Three small things, none blocking: (1) the value-flag list is maintained by hand, so a future flag added without updating it would silently change behavior; a comment or guard test would help. (2) A misspelled command followed by --help now exits 0 with usage instead of an error; harmless and arguably friendly, but scripts relying on a failure exit for bad commands would not notice. (3) Tests do not pin `-h` used as an option value or help appearing after valid flags; the code handles both correctly by inspection. I ran git diff --check on the commit (passes) but did not re-run the test suite; the implementer reports npm test and policy check pass, and independent re-runs belong to the verifier. Safe to proceed pending verification.

findings.message: VALUE_OPTIONS is a hand-maintained duplicate of the string options declared across seven parseArgs calls. It matches today (verified exhaustively), but adding a string option later without updating the set would make `--newopt --help` print usage and exit 0 instead of erroring, and no test would catch it except for --path.
findings.suggestion: Add a comment on VALUE_OPTIONS pointing at the parseArgs call sites, or a test that derives string options from each command's parseArgs definition and asserts the set stays in sync.

findings.message: hasHelpFlag runs before command dispatch, so an unknown command followed by a help flag (e.g. `frobnicate --help`) now prints usage and exits 0 instead of the previous exit-1 'unknown command' error. This is outside the acceptance criteria and is common CLI behavior, but scripts that probe commands and rely on a non-zero exit for a misspelled command would see success.
findings.suggestion: If unknown-command-with-help should remain an error, check the command against the known list before honoring the help flag; otherwise document the behavior.

findings.message: The option-value regression test covers only `--path --help`. Nothing pins `-h` as an option value (e.g. `validate --kind -h`) or a help flag appearing after valid options (e.g. `validate --format json --help`); both behave correctly today by inspection but could regress silently.
findings.suggestion: Add one case asserting a value-position `-h` does not trigger help, and one asserting help still wins when mixed with valid options.

checklist.item: `--help` or `-h` after any command or subcommand prints usage to stdout and exits 0
checklist.notes: Help is handled centrally in main() before the command switch, so all commands share it. The new test exercises both flags against all 16 command/subcommand forms, asserting EXIT.OK, usage text on stdout, and empty stderr.

checklist.item: Unknown options other than --help/-h still fail with exit 1 as before
checklist.notes: Dedicated test asserts `validate --unknown` returns EXIT.ERROR with an 'unknown option' message and no usage on stdout. parseArgs strictness for all other commands is unchanged; verified by diff inspection.
